questions.text: A bucket is in the shape of a frustum of a cone with top radius 28 cm, bottom radius 21 cm and vertical height 24 cm. Taking π = 22/7, what is its capacity?
questions.trap: Using the slant height or the wrong formula.
wrongReasons: Used a cylinder of mean radius 24.5 cm and height 24 cm
Used the slant height in place of the vertical height
Took half of the correct volume

questions.text: The largest possible solid sphere is cut out of a cube of edge 21 cm. Taking π = 22/7, how much material is wasted?
questions.explanation: The sphere's diameter is 21 cm, so r = 10.5 cm. Sphere = 4/3 × 22/7 × 10.5³ = 4,851 cm³. Cube = 9,261 cm³. Wasted = 9,261 − 4,851 = 4,410 cm³.
questions.trap: Giving the volume of the sphere itself.
questions.revise: Largest sphere in a cube: diameter = edge
wrongReasons: Gave the volume of the sphere
Gave the volume of the cube
Used 10 cm as the sphere's radius

questions.text: A rectangular sheet 44 cm by 28 cm is rolled into a cylinder in two ways: once with the 44 cm side as the circumference, and once with the 28 cm side as the circumference. What is the ratio of the volumes of the two cylinders?
steps: Circumference C, height h → V = C²h/(4π)
questions.trap: Squaring the ratio of the sides.
wrongReasons: Inverted the ratio
Squared the ratio of the sides
Assumed the same sheet gives the same volume

questions.text: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and drawn into a wire of circular cross-section with radius 0.2 cm. What is the length of the wire?
questions.explanation: Volume of the sphere = 4/3 π × 216 = 288π. Wire: π × 0.04 × L = 288π, so L = 7,200 cm = 72 m.
questions.trap: Mistaking the unit conversion from cm to m.
wrongReasons: Slipped by a factor of ten when converting cm to m
Used the sphere's diameter in place of the radius
Used 2/3 πr³ instead of 4/3 πr³

questions.text: A cuboid of dimensions 12 cm × 9 cm × 8 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many cubes have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation: Cubes with exactly two painted faces lie along the edges but not at corners: 4[(12 − 2) + (9 − 2) + (8 − 2)] = 4 × (10 + 7 + 6) = 92.
questions.trap: Including the corner cubes.
wrongReasons: Counted the cubes with exactly one face painted
Counted only the corner cubes
Used 4(l + w + h) without removing the corner cubes

questions.text: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 14 cm. Taking π = 22/7, what is the area of the part of the circle that lies outside the square?
questions.explanation: The diagonal of the square is 28 cm, so its area is 28²/2 = 392 cm². Circle area = 22/7 × 196 = 616. Outside part = 616 − 392 = 224 cm².
questions.trap: Using the radius as the side of the square.
wrongReasons: Gave the area of the square
Gave the area of the circle
Used the side 14 cm for the square

questions.text: A conical vessel of base radius 6 cm and height 24 cm is full of water. All the water is poured into a cylindrical vessel of base radius 4 cm. To what height does the water rise?
questions.explanation: Volume of the water = ⅓π × 36 × 24 = 288π. Cylinder: π × 16 × h = 288π, so h = 18 cm.
questions.trap: Leaving out the ⅓ of the cone.
wrongReasons: Gave the height of the cone
Gave the base radius of the cone
Left out the ⅓ and divided by 2

questions.text: The mode of the following distribution is 24. Find the missing frequency x.
questions.explanation: The modal class is 20–30 with f₁ = 12. f₀ = x and f₂ = 9. Mode = 20 + (12 − x)/(24 − x − 9) × 10 = 24, so (12 − x)/(15 − x) = 0.4. Then 12 − x = 6 − 0.4x, so 6 = 0.6x and x = 10.
questions.trap: Misplacing f₀ and f₂.
questions.revise: Mode: L + (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h
wrongReasons: Used the frequency of the class after the modal class
Used the frequency of the modal class
Used the frequency of the class two places after

questions.text: The average marks of 40 students in section A are 72 and of 60 students in section B are 65. A third section C of 20 students is added and the overall average of all 120 students is 68.5. What is the average marks of section C?
questions.explanation: Total marks of all = 120 × 68.5 = 8,220. Section A = 2,880; section B = 3,900. Section C = 8,220 − 2,880 − 3,900 = 1,440. Average = 1,440/20 = 72.
questions.trap: Using the simple mean of the section averages.
wrongReasons: Gave the overall average
Gave the average of section B
Took the simple mean of 72 and 68

questions.text: By what percent did the total sales of the three shops increase from January to March?
questions.trap: Dividing by the later value.
questions.revise: Percent increase uses the earlier value as base
wrongReasons: Compared with March instead of January
Compared with the sales of shop A only
Subtracted the percentages of the shops

questions.text: What is the mean of the distribution shown in the table?
questions.trap: Using the unweighted mean of class marks.
wrongReasons: Took the mean of the class marks unweighted
Added 2 to the correct mean
Took the modal class mark

questions.text: For a moderately skewed distribution, the mean is 34 and the median is 32. What is the approximate mode?
questions.explanation: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean = 96 − 68 = 28.
questions.trap: Reversing the roles of mean and median.
wrongReasons: Took the median minus 2
Took mean + 2
Took the average of mean and median

questions.text: The mean of a set of observations is 12 and the standard deviation is 4. Each observation is multiplied by 3 and then increased by 5. What is the sum of the new mean and the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: New mean = 3 × 12 + 5 = 41. New SD = 3 × 4 = 12, since adding a constant does not change the SD. Sum = 53.
questions.trap: Adding 5 to the standard deviation.
questions.revise: Linear transformation of mean and SD
wrongReasons: Gave only the new mean
Added 5 to the old mean and the old SD
Added 5 to the new SD as well

questions.text: On a certain sum of money, the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹620. What is the sum?
questions.trap: Using the 2-year formula.
wrongReasons: Used 10% as the multiplier
Used 1% instead of 3.1% as the multiplier
Used the formula for 2 years

questions.text: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, and C and A together in 20 days. In how many days can A alone do the work?
questions.explanation: Adding the three rates: 2(A + B + C) = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 12/60 = 1/5, so A + B + C = 1/10. A = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. A alone takes 30 days.
questions.trap: Dividing instead of subtracting rates.
questions.revise: Pairwise work: add all three equations
wrongReasons: Gave the pair time of C and A
Doubled the correct answer
Gave the time taken by all three together

questions.text: A policeman sees a thief 200 m away. The thief runs at 10 km/h and the policeman chases at 11 km/h. How far will the thief run before he is caught?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 1 km/h. Time to close 0.2 km = 0.2 hour. The thief runs 10 × 0.2 = 2 km = 2,000 m.
questions.trap: Giving the policeman's distance.
wrongReasons: Gave the initial gap
Used the policeman's speed times 0.1 hour
Gave the distance run by the policeman

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not vote and 5% of the votes cast were invalid. The winner got 55% of the valid votes and won by 1,710 votes. How many voters were on the voters' list?
questions.explanation: Valid votes = 0.9 × 0.95 = 0.855 of the voters. The winner's margin = 55% − 45% = 10% of valid votes = 0.0855 of the voters. So voters = 1,710 ÷ 0.0855 = 20,000.
questions.trap: Taking the margin as a share of all voters.
wrongReasons: Ignored the 10% who did not vote
Ignored the invalid votes
Treated the margin as 10% of the voters

questions.text: A dealer marks his goods 25% above the cost price and allows a discount of 8%. He also gives only 800 g in place of 1 kg. What is his overall profit percent?
questions.explanation: For goods marked at 25% above cost: price for '1 kg' = 1.25 × 0.92 = 1.15 of the cost of 1 kg. The dealer actually delivers only 0.8 kg costing 0.8. Profit = (1.15 − 0.8)/0.8 = 0.4375 = 43.75%.
questions.trap: Leaving out the false weight.
questions.revise: False weight: cost of what is actually given
wrongReasons: Ignored the false weight
Gave the mark-up only
Used the false weight but ignored the discount

questions.text: In a right-angled triangle with the perpendicular sides 9 cm and 12 cm, what is the distance of the centroid from the vertex at the right angle?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is 15 cm and the median from the right angle is half of it, 7.5 cm. The centroid is ⅔ of the way along the median from the vertex: ⅔ × 7.5 = 5 cm.
questions.trap: Using ⅓ instead of ⅔.
wrongReasons: Gave the median to the hypotenuse
Took ⅓ of the median
Gave the distance to a leg's midpoint

questions.text: Two parallel chords of lengths 16 cm and 12 cm are drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. What is the maximum possible distance between them?
questions.explanation: The distances of the chords from the centre are √(100 − 64) = 6 and √(100 − 36) = 8. If they are on opposite sides, distance = 6 + 8 = 14 cm; on the same side, 8 − 6 = 2 cm. The maximum is 14 cm.
questions.trap: Giving the same-side distance.
wrongReasons: Gave the minimum distance
Gave the diameter
Gave the radius

questions.text: The perpendicular sides of a right-angled triangle are 8 cm and 15 cm. What is the sum of its inradius and circumradius?
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = 17. Circumradius = 17/2 = 8.5. Inradius = (8 + 15 − 17)/2 = 3. Sum = 11.5 cm.
questions.trap: Giving only one of the two radii.
questions.revise: Right triangle: r = (a + b − c)/2, R = c/2
wrongReasons: Gave the circumradius
Gave the inradius
Used (8 + 15)/2 as the inradius

questions.text: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 64°. The bisectors of the exterior angles at B and C meet at a point O. What is the measure of ∠BOC?
questions.explanation: The angle between the bisectors of the exterior angles at B and C is 90° − ∠A/2 = 90° − 32° = 58°.
questions.trap: Using the incentre formula.
wrongReasons: Gave 90° + ∠A/2, the incentre angle
Gave ∠A/2
Gave 180° − ∠A

questions.text: If tan θ + sec θ = 3 and θ is acute, what is the value of sin θ?
questions.explanation: Since sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, secθ − tanθ = 1/3. Adding: 2 sec θ = 10/3, so sec θ = 5/3 and tan θ = 4/3. Then sin θ = tan θ / sec θ = 4/5 = 0.8.
questions.trap: Not using the reciprocal identity.
wrongReasons: Gave cos θ
Mixed up the ratio 4 : 3 with 3 : 4
Gave 1/sin θ

questions.text: A 25 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 7 m from the wall. The top of the ladder slips down the wall by 4 m. How far does the foot of the ladder move away from the wall?
questions.explanation: Initial height = √(625 − 49) = 24 m. After slipping the height is 20 m, so the foot is at √(625 − 400) = 15 m. The foot moves 15 − 7 = 8 m.
questions.trap: Giving the new position instead of the displacement.
wrongReasons: Gave the slip of the top
Gave the new distance of the foot
Gave the original distance of the foot

questions.text: If cosec θ − cot θ = 2, what is the value of cosec θ + cot θ?
questions.explanation: (cosec θ − cot θ)(cosec θ + cot θ) = cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1. So the sum = 1/2 = 0.5.
questions.trap: Taking the sum equal to the difference.
wrongReasons: Took it equal to the given difference
Squared the difference
Took the product 1 as the sum

questions.subtopic: Sum of cubes from sum and product
questions.text: If x + y = 7 and xy = 10, what is the value of x³ + y³?
questions.trap: Adding instead of subtracting 3xy(x + y).
wrongReasons: Cubed the sum without correction
Used + 3xy(x + y)
Gave (x + y)²

questions.text: How many integers satisfy the inequality |2x − 5| < 7?
questions.explanation: −7 < 2x − 5 < 7 gives −2 < 2x < 12, i.e. −1 < x < 6. The integers are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: six values.
questions.trap: Including the end points.
wrongReasons: Included the end value x = 6 or x = −1
Missed the zero
Counted twice for both signs

questions.text: The roots of x² − px + 12 = 0 are positive integers that differ by 1. What is the value of p?
questions.explanation: The roots are 3 and 4 (product 12, difference 1). p is the sum of the roots = 7.
questions.trap: Confusing the sum with the product.
wrongReasons: Took the difference as the sum
Took the product as the sum
Took the sum as 12 + 1

questions.text: The LCM of two numbers is 12 times their HCF and the sum of the HCF and the LCM is 403. If one of the numbers is 93, what is the other?
questions.explanation: HCF + 12 HCF = 403, so HCF = 31 and LCM = 372. Product of the numbers = 31 × 372 = 11,532. Other number = 11,532 ÷ 93 = 124.
questions.trap: Giving the HCF or LCM as the number.
questions.revise: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers
wrongReasons: Gave the HCF
Gave the LCM
Repeated the given number

questions.text: What is the largest 4-digit number which, when divided by 12, 15 and 18, leaves a remainder of 7 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 15, 18) = 180. The largest multiple of 180 below 10,000 is 55 × 180 = 9,900. Add the remainder: 9,907.
questions.trap: Forgetting to add the remainder.
wrongReasons: Left out the remainder
Used the second-largest multiple of 180
Took the largest 4-digit number ending in 7
